Codebook.definition: Quality Assurance is involved in the development process from the beginning to ensure clarity of requirements and reduce bugs.
inclusion_criteria: Text mentions QA involvement at the start of the project or planning phase.
exclusion_criteria: Text mentions QA involvement only at the testing phase.
typical_examples: QA is involved because he will help refine the acceptance criteria.
atypical_examples: The QA team performs testing only after development is complete.
Codebook.relevance_to_RQ: This code addresses how early QA involvement can improve software quality by ensuring requirements clarity and reducing errors.

Codebook.definition: Continuous feedback from various stakeholders is used to refine requirements and improve product quality.
inclusion_criteria: Text mentions receiving and acting upon feedback continuously through the development process.
exclusion_criteria: Feedback is mentioned as one-time or limited to specific phases only.
typical_examples: Continuous feedback helps us to build a better product.
atypical_examples: Feedback is presented only during initial planning.
Codebook.relevance_to_RQ: The code highlights how continuous feedback helps in refining product features for better quality.

Codebook.definition: Collaboration among team members, including knowledge sharing, results in improved code quality and reduced defects.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions collaborative activities that directly impact code quality.
exclusion_criteria: Collaboration is mentioned without relation to quality improvement.
typical_examples: Developers collaborate to learn from each other and write better code.
atypical_examples: Collaboration mentioned but with no mention of quality improvement.
Codebook.relevance_to_RQ: This code demonstrates how Scrum-based collaboration fosters a supportive environment leading to improved software quality.

Codebook.definition: Scrum's transparency ensures that team members are accountable for the quality of their contributions.
inclusion_criteria: References to transparency leading to accountability for work quality.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions of transparency that do not relate to accountability or quality.
typical_examples: Transparency means the quality of each person's work is visible to others.
atypical_examples: Transparency discussed without reference to quality or accountability.
Codebook.relevance_to_RQ: This code explains how the transparency inherent to Scrum processes results in enhanced accountability, which drives quality improvements.

Codebook.definition: Iterative approaches in Scrum allow for quick adjustments and improvement of quality based on regular client feedback.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions iterative development leading to continuous improvements.
exclusion_criteria: Iterative processes mentioned without clear quality improvement results.
typical_examples: Being iterative, adjustments keep quality aligned with client needs.
atypical_examples: Iterative processes discussed but unrelated to quality improvements.
Codebook.relevance_to_RQ: This code supports the understanding of Scrum's iterative approach as a method for enhancing software quality through regular updates and feedback.

Codebook.definition: Automation and testing practices integral to Scrum processes aim to reduce errors and improve software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions automated testing or frequent testing processes.
exclusion_criteria: Testing mentioned but not in the context of automation or quality.
atypical_examples: Testing mentioned briefly without a direct link to quality.
Codebook.relevance_to_RQ: The code details the role of testing and automation in maintaining high quality in Scrum-developed software.
